title: Format a number with two decimals
description: Implement a function called FormatArea that receives a number and returns it as text with exactly two decimal places: FormatArea(72) -> "72.00", FormatArea(3.14159) -> "3.14". Values are rounded rather than truncated: FormatArea(1.239) -> "1.24".
objective: Practice formatting a floating point number as text with a fixed number of decimal places.

metadata.source: Learn Go With Tests - Structs, methods and interfaces (https://quii.gitbook.io/learn-go-with-tests/go-fundamentals/structs-methods-and-interfaces)

title: Declare a Shape interface
description: Declare an interface type called Shape that describes any value having a method called Area which receives nothing and returns a number. Then implement a function called TotalArea that receives a list of Shapes and returns the sum of their areas: TotalArea([shape of area 12, shape of area 4]) -> 16. An empty list totals zero: TotalArea([]) -> 0.
objective: Practice declaring an interface and writing a function that works with any value satisfying it.

title: Make a Circle satisfy Shape
description: Implement a struct type called Circle with a radius field, and a method called Area returning the circle's area, which is pi times the radius squared: Circle(radius: 10).Area() -> 314.16 (to two decimals). Take pi from the standard library's maths package instead of writing the digits yourself. The hidden test also stores a Circle in a variable whose type only requires an Area method, so Circle must satisfy that requirement without you declaring anything extra.
objective: Practice satisfying an interface implicitly by defining the method it requires, and using a standard library constant.

title: Test area across shape types
description: Three shape types are already implemented, along with an interface called Shape that any value with an Area method satisfies. A rectangle's area is width times height: Rectangle(width: 12, height: 6).Area() -> 72. A circle's area is pi times the radius squared: Circle(radius: 10).Area() -> 314.16 (to two decimals). A triangle's area is half of base times height: Triangle(base: 12, height: 6).Area() -> 36. Write one table-driven test whose cases hold Shape values, covering all three kinds of shape.
objective: Practice a table-driven test whose cases hold interface values, so one loop covers several concrete types.
mutant_hints: treats a rectangle as if it were a triangle, reporting half of its real area
leaves the constant pi out of the circle's area
forgets to halve base times height for a triangle
